Run manifest and health
/app/run.json declares install, build and serve; the server listens on port 4173 or APP_PUBLIC_PORT; and GET /api/health answers as published in Server boundary.

Local accounts and roles
People sign in with a seeded username and password, land on the home screen of their first role in the published precedence, and reach only the screens and actions that the published role-to-screen and baseline access tables grant any of their roles, with a forbidden screen showing the published outcome.

One error order and shape
Every API error uses the one published error body and the published check order, and idempotent replays are answered before any state check.

Grading route and server clock
The key-guarded grading route creates any published fixture, saves as any user with a chosen version, changes runtime limits, redirects storage, and sets or advances the server clock, running all due background work before it answers.

Expression language
Every condition in rules, policies, SLA definitions, assignment, workflows and filters is written in the published expression language, and a malformed expression is refused with the published column error.

Published breakpoints
The ticket workspace and the requester portal show three panes at 1280x800, two at 768x1024 and one at 375x812, switching exactly at 1024 and 768 pixels wide, with no horizontal page overflow.

Published empty and not-found states
Empty queues, empty filter results, knowledge searches with no results, an empty inbox, no waiting votes and unknown pages each show their published single line and one button, character for character.

Server boundary and limits
The server serves only its own origin, refuses oversize bodies and cross-origin writes with the published bodies, never serves source or credentials, and enforces the published rate limits.

Hero poster
The landing screen is the published pinned-title poster: the giant product name on the orange field over six procedural service portraits, with the wordmark, Menu, sentence and button in their corners.

Pinned subject screens
Every working screen pins its subject's name in the display face on the orange field above white working sections, with square corners, status shown as words plus solid ink blocks, tabular figures and comfortable tap targets.

Source integrity
Credentials and URLs are read from the environment, conditions are interpreted from the published language without evaluating code, and each derived value is computed once on the server.

Record lifecycles and numbering
Incidents, problems, changes, request items and tasks move only along their published transition tables, illegal moves answer 422 with the published message, and numbers use the published prefixes with no gaps from rejected saves.

Priority matrix and override
Priority follows the published impact and urgency table with the business-critical bump, and only the operator may override it with a reason, which shows the published badge and writes an audit entry.

Knowledge search and suggestions
Knowledge search, and the suggestions shown while someone types a short description, rank published, in-audience, unexpired articles by the published formula.

Keyboard incident journey
From the incident grid, the operator opens, edits and moves an incident through its states using only the keyboard, while the requester's portal page updates and announces each change without a reload.

Business time across daylight saving
Elapsed business time counts only the open hours of the schedule's local days, skips holidays, and stays exact across the 29 March 2026 and 25 October 2026 clock changes in Europe/Berlin.

SLA pause, priority swap and reopen
The pause state stops the clock, a priority change swaps the SLA and recalculates it from the original start, and a reopen resumes from the elapsed time at resolve, all by the published rules.

SLA thresholds on the server clock
Crossing 50, 75 and 100 percent of a target fires the published inbox actions and the breach flag once each, whether time passes in real time or because the server clock was advanced.

Countdown from server time
Every SLA countdown in the browser comes from the last server message plus the browser clock's elapsed delta, so a wrong device clock never changes what is shown, and only the server declares pause, resume or breach.

SLA journey
An agent and a requester watch one incident's SLA through hold, priority change, escalation, breach, resolve and reopen across a holiday, and both countdowns agree throughout.

Per-field versions and presence
Saves carry each field's last-seen version: saves to different fields merge, a stale save to a changed field answers 409 with both values, work notes always append, presence lists who is viewing, and every change is audited with before and after values.

Business rules
Business rules run in the published timing and order, detect field changes, abort saves with their own message without using up a number, and stop at the published nesting limit.

Shared incident journey
Two people on one incident see each other present, save different fields, settle a same-field conflict in the published dialog by keyboard, and watch notes and activity arrive live.

Assignment rules and round robin
A new record goes to the group of the first matching assignment rule and then, by round robin, to the next member who is under capacity and not out of office, or to Triage with the published activity line.

Rotations across daylight saving
Weekly rotations hand over at 09:00 in the schedule's zone across daylight saving changes, and one-off overrides take precedence by the published rule.

Escalation ladder and late acknowledge
An unacknowledged page climbs the ladder when the server clock passes each level's acknowledge timer, an acknowledge stops it, and a late acknowledge is recorded with the published text.

Closed drawers and sheets are inert
At 375x812 and 768x1024, a closed navigation drawer, filter sheet or action sheet is invisible, cannot take focus and is absent from the accessibility tree until it is opened again.

On-call journey
A record is assigned automatically, a page escalates on the server clock, the backup technician acknowledges from a phone by long press or swipe, and the operator's desk and inbox update live.

Classes and loop-free relationships
Configuration items inherit attributes by the published class tree, relationships use the closed type list, and a relationship that would form a dependency loop is refused with the published chain message.

Layered map and node keyboard
The service map places each item at its published layered coordinates and gives each node its published accessible name; arrow keys move focus between nodes by the published rule, and Enter expands a node with the published animation.

Impact spread
Marking an item down or degraded spreads along dependency relationships; a cluster stays degraded while its required healthy members remain, a maintenance window stops the spread, and each affected person counts once.

Service map journey
By keyboard, the operator adds items and relationships, meets the loop refusal, marks an outage, and watches it stop at a degraded cluster and behind a maintenance window, with node labels and animations as published.

Major incident proposal
An outage that reaches the published threshold proposes a major incident that only the operator can promote or reject, and promotion links the open incidents on affected items as children.

Resolve together
Resolving a major incident resolves every open child in one transaction with the parent's code and note, or changes none of them, and a child can be reopened alone.

Outage relay
The relay pins the failed item's name and scrolls one panel per affected item in the server's order, with a people counter that rises and falls with scroll; under reduced motion it becomes a static list with the total announced once.

Outage relay look
Relay panels are full-height poster panels, each with its item's procedural portrait, its relationship path and a flat ground in its tier colour, under the pinned failed-item name.

Problems and workarounds
Problems link incidents, a published workaround appears live on every linked open incident, and a problem resolves and closes by the published closure rule.

Major incident journey
An outage proposes a major incident that is promoted and gets its children; two people follow the shared timeline live, resolve together, reopen one child alone, and see a workaround arrive on the open children.

Change models and risk score
Normal, standard and emergency changes follow their own transition tables, and the risk score and band follow the published formula and route each change to its approval steps.

Freeze and overlap refusal
A change inside a freeze window, or overlapping another change on the same item or on an item linked to it by dependency, is refused with the published message.

Locked fields reset approval
Editing a locked field after approval has started returns the change to Assessed, voids every vote, writes the published activity line, and removes the vote from approvers' open screens live.

Change calendar keyboard
The change calendar moves by day with the arrow keys and by month with PageUp and PageDown, opens a day with Enter, and returns focus to that day on Escape.

Change journey
The operator drafts a normal change, sees its risk score, meets the freeze and dependency overlap refusals, gets it approved, resets approval by editing a locked field while the approver watches, and navigates the calendar by keyboard.

Quorum, delegates and late votes
Each approval step closes by its published quorum rule or its window, a delegate's vote counts once for the member, a rejection resets later steps, and a late or repeated vote is refused.

Operator-only actions
Publishing workflows, committing or backing out configuration sets, closing a vote early and every other operator-only endpoint refuse all other roles with the published 403 body.

Phone voting gestures
On a 375-pixel-wide phone, an approver approves by swiping right or rejects by swiping left past the published distance, with an Undo period, or opens the vote action sheet with a long press.

Inbox rules and digest
Inbox items follow the published event rules and each person's digest setting, and the unread count updates live.

Board journey
A live agenda, weighted and N of M votes from two people with a live tally, a delegate's vote, a rejection that resets later steps, a phone swipe with Undo, and the result delivered to the inbox.

Catalog variables and order guides
Catalog items offer typed variables with dependent choices, and order guides add the published items for the answers given.

Form policies on both sides
Form policies make fields mandatory, visible or read-only in the browser as values change, and the server enforces the same policies with the published field errors.

Cart checkout
Checking out the cart creates one request, one request item per line and the tasks from each item's workflow, and a replay with the same idempotency key returns the stored response.

Catalog journey
A requester orders through the order guide and the cart with dependent choices and policies, the approver signs off, and the portal tracks each item and task live to Delivered.

Designer by keyboard
The workflow designer adds, moves, reorders and deletes steps, branches and loops using only the keyboard, with the published focus rules and step-move animation.

Versions, runs and flow limits
Publishing creates a numbered version while runs stay on the version they started on; self-calling subflows and runaway loops stop with the published messages, and failed steps can be retried or handled.

Designer journey
The operator builds a flow by keyboard with a branch and a loop, meets the loop-limit and subflow-chain errors, publishes version 2 while a run stays on version 1, and retries a failed step while a second person watches the run live.

Access rule evaluation
Table, row and field rules apply in the published order: a hidden record answers 404, and a denied field write on a visible record answers 403.

Denied fields leave no trace
A denied field or row is absent from lists, forms, search, activity, reports, dashboards, exports and group counts, and filtering or grouping on a denied field is refused as an unknown field.

Impersonation and live role change
Operator impersonation shows the published banner and writes an audit entry, and a role or rule change reaches the affected person's open pages without a reload.

Access journey
A field rule and a row rule take effect for a department manager on every surface, impersonation shows what the manager sees, and a role change reaches the manager's open page live.

Condition builder and filter text
The condition builder edits grouped AND and OR conditions with reference paths by keyboard, and round-trips exactly with the published filter text.

Group counts, paging, notices and bulk update
Lists group with counts, page with the published tie-break, announce new matching records instead of inserting them, and report bulk updates row by row.

Dashboards
Dashboard widgets compute the published aggregates on the server in the viewer's time zone, update live, offer a data table alternative and drill down to the filtered list.

Lists journey
The operator builds a nested filter by keyboard, round-trips its text, groups, bulk-updates with a partial failure, sees the new-records notice when someone else creates a record, and drills down from a live widget in another time zone.

Import format and re-runs
Imports in the published format preview each row's action and errors with line numbers, update by match key instead of duplicating, and change nothing when run again.

Configuration sets
Test workspace changes are captured in a named set, exported to storage, previewed against live with collisions, committed with per-item choices and backed out exactly.

Storage-confirmed files and exports
Attachments, import files, export files and configuration set files count as stored only after storage accepts the object under its published key, and only then does an export show complete.

Storage outage and recovery
While storage is unreachable, record work continues, the published banners and 503 body appear and uploads queue; when storage returns, queued uploads finish, failed exports retry and the banner clears without a restart.

Import and promotion journey
The operator imports a file with line errors, re-runs it with no changes, promotes and backs out a configuration set, and runs an export through a storage outage while record work continues.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is needed to start the app.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package, meaning the production dependency tree (npm ls --omit=dev --all --json), with its licence, plus the Unbounded and Onest fonts.
Every shipped package and asset is under MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or, for fonts, OFL-1.1.
The only datastores are the provided Postgres and MinIO: no SQLite or other database files, no in-process persistent store, no cache or queue server.
Fonts, images and scripts are served from the app's own origin, and the browser makes no request to any other origin.
No user-supplied text is ever run as code: there is no eval, new Function, vm module or dynamic import of user data.
package-lock.json is committed, and install uses it.
The provided development service configuration (the compose files and their seeded credentials) is left unchanged.
